clue.text: Party returning me out of fashion

indicators.note: out here means the word me sits outside, around the other piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: returning means the word for a party is read from right to left

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A partygoer heading home feels hopelessly unfashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses the party word and 'out' sets ME around it; 'of' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mode is a current style or vogue, the prevailing way of dressing or doing things.

clue.text: Chamois ran amok, intoxicated by it?

indicators.note: running amok is wild behaviour, so the letters of chamois ran are thrown about

explanation.surface: A mountain goat runs wild, drunk on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amok' rearranges CHAMOIS RAN; the definition asks what might make one tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Maraschino is a cherry liqueur, an alcoholic drink one could get tipsy on.

clue.text: Belief of master led by pointer, for example

indicators.note: led by means the master piece follows the dog piece

parts.note: a pointer is a breed of dog
MA is a Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A master following his pointer dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'led by' puts the dog in front of the master, as a pointer would walk ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a fixed set of beliefs or doctrine held by a church or group.

clue.text: Apparently is stolen by error

indicators.note: error suggests the letters of the preceding words have gone wrong and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something has seemingly been stolen through a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'error' rearranges the ten letters of IS STOLEN BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensibly means seemingly or as it appears on the face of things, so it matches apparently.

clue.text: General confusion of the increase with a decrease

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'General confusion of the increase with a decrease (7)': anagram of INCREASE less A gives SINCERE, but 'General' does not define it; likely OCR for 'Genuine', more than three letters off, and no scan.
annotationWithheld.clue: General confusion of the increase with a decrease

clue.text: Oriental festival on first of November

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of November is taken

explanation.surface: An Eastern festival held on the first day of November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link placing N after EASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental means from the East, as in Asian or eastern lands.

clue.text: From here, emergency appeal received in the morning

indicators.note: received means the distress signal takes in the morning abbreviation

parts.note: SOS is the Morse distress signal
a.m. means in the morning

explanation.surface: An emergency call received at dawn from a distant place.
explanation.walkthrough: Samos is a Greek island; 'From here' defines it as a place one may come from.
explanation.definitionFit: Samos is a Greek island in the Aegean, so a place one can be from.

clue.text: Dawn, order Ben double gin

indicators.note: order suggests sorting the letters into a new arrangement
double asks for two measures, so the word gin is written out twice

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: At daybreak, someone orders a double gin for Ben.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a request at the bar, but it rearranges the letters of BEN and GIN twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is the start of the day, so it means the onset or start of something.

clue.text: Hear why go back, adopting strange attitudes?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Hear why go back, adopting strange attitudes? (4)': sound of 'why' (Y) plus GO reversed (OG) gives YOG; nothing supplies the final I, so the clue looks cut short in OCR and no scan.

clue.text: I climb around with egghead, at loose end — being stupid

indicators.note: around suggests the letters being shifted about into a new order

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of egg

indicators.note: end means only the final letter of loose is taken

explanation.surface: Someone clambers about with an intellectual, at a loose end, acting foolishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual but gives E, the first letter of egg; 'around' rearranges I CLIMB plus that E into IMBECIL, and 'end' adds the E closing loose.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbecile is a foolish or idiotic person, so the word used as an adjective means stupid.

clue.text: Get miners retrained for the army

indicators.note: retrained suggests the miners being reshaped, so the letters of get miners are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pit workers are retrained to become soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrained' rearranges GET MINERS; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Regiments are the permanent units that make up an army, so collectively they stand for it.

clue.text: Should he lose his master he'd still have his mate

definitions.text: Should he lose his master he'd still have his mate

parts.words: Should he lose his master he'd still have his mate
parts.note: taking away MA, the usual abbreviation for master (of arts), leaves the name of the giant's legendary partner in the London Guildhall pair

explanation.surface: A loyal servant whose master dies still has a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: Gog and Magog are the twin giants whose effigies stand in London's Guildhall; drop MA (master) from the answer and his mate Gog remains.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue describes the giant of Guildhall legend, one of a famous pair, whose name minus a master abbreviation gives his partner.

clue.text: Sun overhead? This is what you need

definitions.text: Sun overhead? This is what you need

parts.words: Sun overhead? This is what you need
parts.note: when the midday sun beats down from above, the remedy is somewhere sheltered from its glare

explanation.surface: Advice for a blazing hot day.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelter from direct sunlight is what is wanted when the sun blazes overhead.

clue.text: It's odds-on the key being of service

parts.note: evens is a betting price, odds of one to one
taken as written
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: A gambler thinks a bet in a certain key is a sure thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odds-on' looks like one betting term, but it splits into two pieces; 'It's' and 'being of' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening service of prayer, also called vespers.

clue.text: Encourage to like square meal at breakfast?

parts.note: to egg on is to encourage
taken as written
as means like
a T-square is a drawing tool, giving T

explanation.surface: A recommendation for a hearty morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square meal' looks like one idea, but 'square' gives T and 'meal at breakfast' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg on toast is a classic breakfast dish of a cooked egg served on toasted bread.

clue.text: Shop around for something cooling, as a last resort

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of the word shop being turned about into a new order

parts.note: ice is used for cooling drinks or food

explanation.surface: Someone shops about for a cold treat as a final option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' suggests a holiday spot; here it means an option. 'around' rearranges the shop letters; 'for' and 'as' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospice cares for the terminally ill, so it is the place people go at the very end of life.

clue.text: Went to court about besmirching that was continuous

indicators.note: about means the word for went to court goes around the other piece

parts.note: sued means went to court
a stain is a besmirching, or blot

explanation.surface: Someone sued over constant slander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that was' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sustained means kept up without a break, unbroken over a period.

clue.text: One way of ensuring that colours stay fast

definitions.text: One way of ensuring that colours stay fast

parts.words: One way of ensuring that colours stay fast
parts.note: colours here are a ship's flag; fixing them to the mast with hammer and metal spikes means they cannot be struck in surrender

explanation.surface: A laundry tip for keeping dyes from running.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests dyes not running in the wash; the idiom is nailing one's colours to the mast, refusing to surrender.
explanation.definitionFit: Hammering a flag to the mast makes it impossible to lower, the gesture of defiance in the naval idiom.

clue.text: Our silly broadcast? That's just a fantasy!

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of our silly are spread and reordered

explanation.surface: A silly radio show dismissed as pure fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges OUR SILLY; 'That's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Illusory means based on illusion, unreal or deceptive.

clue.text: Scramble from it, perhaps, on a rainy day?

definitions.text: Scramble from it, perhaps, on a rainy day?

parts.words: Scramble from it, perhaps, on a rainy day?
parts.note: the breakfast sense of scramble points at a hen's product, but the phrase means savings kept back for hard times

explanation.surface: Cooking advice for a wet morning.
explanation.walkthrough: One reading has eggs scrambled; the other is money saved 'for a rainy day', which one may scramble to draw on.
explanation.definitionFit: Savings put aside for future emergencies are proverbially kept for a rainy day.

clue.text: Fish no longer fresh put in storage

parts.note: gar is a long-snouted fish
aged means old, no longer fresh

explanation.surface: Stale fish put away in storage.
explanation.definitionFit: A car garaged is kept in a garage, so stored under cover.

clue.text: Quick movement — or legal action!

indicators.note: action suggests the letters being set in motion and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A sudden step, or else a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' rearranges OR and LEGAL together.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegro is a brisk, lively piece or part of a symphony, a fast movement in music.

clue.text: Everyone getting well again, thanks to the Valerian

parts.note: all means everyone
to heal is to get well again

explanation.surface: Everyone recovers thanks to a herbal remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thanks to' is a link. Valerian is a medicinal herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Allheal is an old folk name for valerian, a plant thought to cure many ills.

clue.text: Group role-playing makes one flag

parts.note: a band is a group of people or musicians

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of the word role being toyed with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A group playing parts produces a banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges ROLE into EROL; 'makes one' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A banderol is a long narrow pennant or streamer flown from a mast or lance.

clue.text: Grounds for medico putting out distress call

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: putting out suggests the signal letters being disrupted into a new order

parts.note: SOS is the Morse distress signal

explanation.surface: A doctor sends a distress call for some reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds' looks like reasons, but means dregs. 'putting out' rearranges SOS into OSS; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is waste or worthless sediment, like the grounds left in a coffee pot.

clue.text: Swan caught in the street is exhausted

indicators.note: caught in means the female swan is held inside the abbreviation for street

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: A swan trapped in a road is worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swan' suggests the bird generally, but a female swan is a PEN; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent describes something used up or tired out, with no energy left.

clue.text: Is she French, from the north?

definitions.text: Is she French, from the north?

parts.note: elle is French for she

explanation.surface: A question about whether a woman is a northern French person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the' is a link. The whole clue is the definition: a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen is a woman's given name, so it fits a question asking who she is.

clue.text: This is marked with across

parts.note: read 'across' as 'a cross': a symbol drawn as one, the addition sign

explanation.surface: A crossword instruction about which way a clue goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' splits into 'a cross', the shape of the addition sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The plus sign is drawn as a small upright cross.

clue.text: Slow scoring rate? Fast for the most part

indicators.note: the most part means only most of the word for fast is kept, its last letter removed

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting before Easter
to can mean for, as in a gift to someone

explanation.surface: A batsman scoring slowly while mostly fasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoring' means written in a musical score, not cricket runs; 'the most part' cuts LENT to LEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lento is the tempo marking on a musical score telling players to perform slowly.

clue.text: Rule a girl may be partisan

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters of rule a girl could be arranged into another word

explanation.surface: A girl's rule might be biased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges RULE A GIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan in the wartime sense is an irregular resistance fighter, the same as a guerrilla.

clue.text: Requires both legs on near side-teams become confused

definitions.text: Requires both legs on near side

parts.note: sides are teams in a game
to addle is to become muddled or confused

explanation.surface: A horsey rule about one side, with teams getting muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side-teams' looks like one word, but 'side' ends the definition and 'teams' gives SIDES.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding sidesaddle means sitting with both legs on the horse's left, the near side.

clue.text: Snap back — get insect!

indicators.note: back means the word for snap is read in reverse

parts.note: tang is a sharp, biting quality, like snap or zest

explanation.surface: A command to swat a fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TANG around; 'get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small two-winged fly, a type of tiny biting creature.
